specification.problem: Use the one-query Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm to identify a completely specified linear Boolean function with certainty, a two-query variant to identify whether a Boolean function is affine (and recover it), and apply both as bounded-error quantum algorithms (success probability at least 2/3) to certain classes of incompletely defined linear and affine Boolean functions.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the problem and a small finite-instance equation set; the two-query circuit details and the incompletely defined function classes are not given in the abstract and are left unspecified.

symbols.meaning: phase or standard oracle for f

equations.label: Linear function
equations.description: Linear Boolean function targeted by the one-query algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: identify a completely specified linear Boolean function
equations.justification: Standard definition of a linear Boolean function, matching the abstract's phrase.
assumptions: Linear means over GF(2) with no constant term

equations.label: Affine function
equations.description: Affine Boolean function targeted by the two-query algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: if the provided Boolean function is affine
equations.justification: Standard definition of an affine function over GF(2).
assumptions: Affine means linear plus constant b

equations.label: BV phase oracle output
equations.description: After Hadamards, a phase-oracle query on a linear function yields |a> deterministically.

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register queried in superposition; holds a after the final Hadamards for linear f

registers.name: anc
registers.role: ancilla in |-> for phase kickback if a standard oracle is used

specification.initial_state: |0>^n (plus ancilla |1> then Hadamard to |-> if standard oracle)

steps.description: One-query BV: apply H^{⊗n} to |0^n>, query the phase oracle once, apply H^{⊗n}, giving |a> for linear f.

Two-query variant for affine f (assumed structure, not given in abstract): run the BV circuit twice, each with one oracle query, so the two outputs can be compared to determine whether f is affine and to recover a and b. The exact second-query construction is unspecified.

specification.measurement: Measure the n-qubit input register in the computational basis after the final Hadamards. For completely specified linear f the outcome is a with certainty. For the two-query variant, measure after each query round (assumed structure).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Linear case: output the measured string as a. Affine case (assumed): compare the two outcomes to decide whether f is affine and recover a and b. Incompletely defined case: accept the output as correct with probability of success at least 2/3, and repeat or take a majority vote if needed; the exact rule is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Standard GF(2) definitions of linear and affine functions used
Second query's circuit is an assumed repetition of the BV circuit, not taken from the abstract
Second query is a repetition or variant of the BV circuit
Measurement is in the computational basis on the input register
Postprocessing rule for affinity decision is assumed
